column1: # What the interop suite runs and what it expects. interop/run.mbtx reads it.
#   side    client: gaato/mttp's Client against a third-party server
#           server: gaato/mttp's server driven by a third-party client
#           (interop/clients/*), directly or through a reverse proxy.
#   case    the case id the program understands
#   where   which runs the row applies to. Client side:
#           <runtime>/<server>/<scheme>, with runtime native, node, bun or
#           deno (js under that host), server nginx, caddy or apache, scheme
#           http or https. Server side: <client>/<target>, with client curl,
#           go, httpx, node, bun, deno or raw (Python raw-socket probes),
#           target direct, nginx, caddy or apache. Each part is `*` or
#   expect  pass: the case must pass.
#           known: the case shows a documented third-party quirk; it is
#           reported as KNOWN with the note, and fails the run if it passes,
#           so that a pin update that fixes the quirk updates this row.
#           n/a: not run; the note says why.
#   note    why, for known and n/a
# For one case and run the last matching row decides, so a general row comes
# first and its exceptions after it. A case with no matching row is not run.
# Client side: gaato/mttp's Client against nginx, Caddy and Apache.

column1: # Server side: third-party clients against gaato/mttp's server,
# directly and behind nginx, Caddy and Apache.

column5: Node's fetch (undici) sends a request issued right after a body was read on a second connection, then alternates between the two; it does the same against nginx and Caddy (X-Conn alternates 1, 2, 1, 2), and reuses one connection when the requests are a few milliseconds apart, so the server keeps the connection alive and the choice is undici's

column1: # directly as the mttp documentation says, and through each proxy either

column5: Caddy (Go net/http) reads a request with both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding by Transfer-Encoding, as RFC 9112 section 6.3 allows, but keeps the connection open where that section says MUST close it, so the bytes after the chunked body are read as the next request (src/net/http/transfer.go, fixLength). Each request reaches the mttp server well framed; the server refuses the same bytes sent directly

nginx skips only spaces, not tabs, before a field value (src/http/ngx_http_parse.c, sw_space_before_value), so "Transfer-Encoding:<TAB>chunked" is an unknown coding to it and it answers 501; RFC 9110 section 5.6.3 allows the tab. A refusal, so nothing ambiguous reaches the server
